actions.oldValue: As jukebox musicals go, though, this one is a badly broken record.
actions.newValue: If you’re willing to pay Broadway prices to see Mr. Cranston give a tremendous performance, there’s a chance you’ll go home happy.
BRO-4599: Network section is negative-mixed: musty period piece, supporting cast lacks force, but Cranston tremendous.

actions.oldValue: Both are eminently worth a visit.
actions.newValue: Running 110 minutes without an intermission, the evening adds up to less than the sum of its parts. But as a showcase for its trio of talented actors, it works beautifully.
BRO-4599: New Born section is mixed-positive: first two monologues slight or overstuffed, Jackman's third strong; evening less than sum of parts but good actor showcase.

actions.oldValue: More familiar but a bit less successful, Mathias’ “Godot” needs a shot of dread.
actions.newValue: McKellen’s silent slow-burn response speaks volumes. He’s got one of the most expressive faces, voices and command of body language on the planet.
BRO-4599: No Man's Land section is positive: stars and supporting cast praised, no reservations stated.

actions.oldValue: Both Land and Godot, in fact, prove that the most challenging and unsettling material can make for accessible, even buoyant, entertainment.
actions.newValue: Hirst, played here by a marvelously deadpan Stewart, listens and drinks while Spooner — McKellen, exquisite in his poised buffoonery — babbles on.
BRO-4599: Critic gives No Man's Land 3.5 of 4 stars (upper 4/5 band); section is positive.
